title: promote-release.mjs: rollback may only undo this promotion, and a failed tag move is included in the restore
description: Found by lore-cli's adversarial review of its mirror of promote-release.mjs at eb1d9f46, 2026-09-27. Mirrored here so the pair stays one mechanism (Article 3.6). S1: --rollback moves latest to whatever priorLatest a record names, and record validation only checks kind, the package list and that priorLatest is a string. So a hand-written priorLatest ("release-candidate", or an unqualified "0.12.0") moves latest onto something no receipt gated, and an old release's record rolled back after a later promotion silently downgrades latest. S2: when one package's dist-tag add fails, possibly after the registry applied it (a timeout), promote() restores only the tags it knows it moved, so that package can stay on the new version while the output says restored.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A record whose priorLatest is not strict semver, or equals the record version, is refused
--rollback refuses unless every package's current latest equals the record version or its recorded priorLatest, so it can only undo this promotion; an unreadable tag set refuses
A dist-tag failure part way through restores the failed package as well as those already moved
Tests cover each case, and a mutation control shows they fail without the fix

finalSummary:
Mirrors lore-cli's two findings from its adversarial review of its copy of promote-release.mjs (eb1d9f46), so the pair stays one mechanism.

S1:
- validateRecord refuses a priorLatest that is not strict semver (catching "release-candidate", "v9.8.0" and "9.8") or that equals the record version.
- New checkRollbackState runs before any --rollback write. It refuses unless every package's current latest is the record version or its recorded prior, so a rollback can only undo that record's promotion and an old record cannot downgrade latest after it moved on. An unreadable tag set refuses.
- Rollback is still not gated on the pair receipt, as QCLI-388 AC3 requires.

S2: on a mid-way dist-tag failure, promote() restores the failed package as well as those already moved, because the write may have landed before the error. Restoring a tag that never moved is a no-op.

Verified:
- test/qcli390-promote-rollback-hardening.test.ts, 7 tests. They include a flaky setTag that applies the write and then throws ETIMEDOUT; before the fix it left that package on the new version.
- Mutation: reverting the S2 filter and removing the semver check turned 2 tests red, the tag-name test and the S2 test. I had predicted 3. The equals-version test exercises a separate branch the mutation did not touch, so the miss was in my prediction, not the suite.
- bun run check exit 0, 774 tests. lore check clean.
